\begin{figure}[htbp]
  \centering
  \resizebox{0.62\linewidth}{!}{%
\ctikzset{bipoles/length=0.95cm, resistors/scale=0.9, capacitors/scale=0.9}
\begin{circuitikz}[
    every node/.append style={font=\footnotesize},
    nlab/.style={font=\scriptsize, inner sep=1.5pt},
    railnode/.style={circle, fill=black, inner sep=1.05pt},
  ]
\draw (0,0) node[railnode]{} node[nlab, above=3pt]{\texttt{CE}}
      to[R, l=$R_{\mathrm{ce}}$] (2.4,0);
\draw (2.4,0) node[railnode]{} node[nlab, above=3pt]{\texttt{RE}}
      to[R, l=$R_u$] (4.8,0);
\node[railnode] at (4.8,0){};
\node[nlab, anchor=south east, inner sep=2.5pt] at (4.72,0.06){$\mathrm{WE_s}$};
\draw (4.8,0) -- (4.8,0.85);
\draw (4.8,0.85) to[R, l=$R_{\mathrm{ct}}$] (7.6,0.85);
\draw (7.6,0.85) -- (7.6,0);
\draw (4.8,0) -- (4.8,-0.85);
\draw (4.8,-0.85) to[C, l_=$C_{\mathrm{dl}}$] (7.6,-0.85);
\draw (7.6,-0.85) -- (7.6,0);
\draw (7.6,0) node[railnode]{} -- (8.5,0) node[nlab, right]{\texttt{WE}};
\end{circuitikz}
  }
  \caption[{Three-electrode cell model.}]{Three-electrode cell model, the load the potentiostat actually drives. \(R_{\mathrm{ce}}\) is the solution resistance from the counter to the reference electrode and \(R_u\) the uncompensated resistance from the reference to the working-electrode surface; the interface itself is the charge-transfer resistance \(R_{\mathrm{ct}}\) in parallel with the double-layer capacitance \(C_{\mathrm{dl}}\). Values are given in Table~\ref{tab:analog-models}. The model is lumped, linear and frequency-independent (no Warburg diffusion term and no potential dependence), so it represents small-signal behaviour about a bias point rather than a full electrochemical response.}
  \label{fig:randles-cell}
\end{figure}
